questions.q:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

I want to buy the less expensive bike, but with the best mileage.
questions.s:
The underlined phrase "less expensive" is incorrect because the sentence implies a superlative comparison (paired with "best mileage"). The superlative form "least" is required when comparing three or more items.

The correct sentence is: I want to buy the least expensive bike, but with the best mileage.

Least-The superlative form, correct for comparing multiple bikes.

Little-An adjective or quantifier for small amounts, not a comparative for "expensive."

Lesser-A comparative form, but less common and not standard for "expensive."

Most less-Grammatically incorrect; "most" and "less" cannot combine.

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

questions.q: As per the study, mosquito-borne/ dengue fever infects little/ 400 million people annually. (SSC CHSL Tier-01 13/03/23)
questions.s: 'Little' is for uncountable nouns. For countable nouns like 'people', 'few' (or 'many') is appropriate.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Prescription safety glasses provide the ______ tailored protection for individuals with vision correction needs.
questions.s:
It can be noted that the sentence establishes that 'prescription safety glasses' is the ultimate option for people who need vision correction, indicating that the sentence is in superlative degree. Thus, the superlative adjective "finest" is appropriate to indicate the highest degree of tailored protection. "Finer" is comparative, "fine" is positive, and "more finely" is an adverb, which doesn't fit the context.

The complete sentence: Prescription safety glasses provide the finest tailored protection for individuals with vision correction needs.

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

Note:

· The Positive Degree is used to denote the mere existence of some quality of what we speak about. It is used when no comparison is made.

· The Comparative degree denotes a higher degree of quality than the positive and is used when two things are compare4.

· The Superlative degree indicates the highest degree of quality and is used when more than two things (or sets of things) are compared.

Opinion → Size → Age → Shape → Colour → Material → Purpose → Noun

questions.q:
Select the sentence that has a grammatical error.

(SSC MTS 2024 S.19_15-Oct_Shift-2)
o: There is a man sitting beside cat.
She saw an excellent episode of the series.
After a tiring day, I had a cup of coffee with Sudhir.
She asked an easy question, and I took an hour to crack it.
questions.s:
Correct Answer: There is a man sitting beside cat.

Explanation:
The sentence is missing an article before "cat".
It should be: "There is a man sitting beside a cat."

All other sentences are grammatically correct.
Hence, the error lies in the first sentence.

questions.q: This shirt is (a)/comparatively better (b)/than that (c)/we saw in corner shop yesterday. (d)
We are interesting in purchasing (a)/ the new laptop model since (b)/ it has many features (c)/ unavailable in conventional computers. (d)/ No error (e)
questions.s: Use "We are interested in" (past participle as adjective) instead of "interesting in.”

questions.q: It is well known / that Mrs. Indira Gandhi / was the first politician / of her time.
questions.s: Explanation:- Use ‘foremost’ in place of ‘first’ kyunki first ka matlab hota hai 'sabse pehla' aur foremost ka matlab hota hai 'us time me sabse mashoor' toh yahan sentence ke meaning ke according 'foremost' ka use hoga.

questions.q: She dances (a) / more gracefully (b) / than her sister. (c) / No error (d)
questions.s: There is no error. 'More gracefully' is correct for comparative degree with adverbs. Answer: (d). Sentence mein koi galti nahi, 'more gracefully' adverb ke liye sahi hai. Jawab: (d).

questions.q: Can you please/pass me that / glittery pen black?
questions.s: Adjectives typically follow a certain order: opinion, size, shape, color, origin, material, purpose. In this case, "glittery" is a type of material/appearance, and "black" is a color. The correct order would be "glittery black pen".

questions.q: He runs (a) / more faster (b) / than I. (c) / No error (d)
questions.s: The error is in part (b). 'Faster' is already comparative; 'more' is redundant. Correct form is 'faster than.' Answer: (b). 'Faster' pehle se comparative hai, 'more' extra hai. Sahi form hai 'faster than.' Jawab: (b).

questions.q: This is (a) / a most unique (b) / design. (c) / No error (d)
questions.s: The error is in part (b). 'Unique' is absolute; 'most unique' is incorrect. Correct form is 'a unique design.' Answer: (b). 'Unique' absolute hai, 'most unique' galat hai. Sahi form hai 'a unique design.' Jawab: (b).
